# API Reference — planr dashboard (SPEC-016)

The dashboard server (`lib/dashboard/server.mjs`) exposes six HTTP routes, all
bound to `127.0.0.1:<port>` (localhost only). All JSON responses use
`Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.

The full user-facing command reference (flags, how-it-works, relationship to
`/status`) lives at [`docs/dashboard.md`](../../docs/dashboard.md) — this file
documents only the HTTP surface for engineers integrating with or extending the
server.

---

## GET /api/graph

Returns the complete typed project graph for the current `.planr/` directory.

**Response** — `200 application/json` — shape matches `schemas/v1.0.0/graph.schema.json`:

```
{
  "nodes": [
    {
      "id": "SPEC-016",
      "type": "spec",           // epic | feature | story | task | spec | backlog | quick | sprint | adr
      "title": "Visual project dashboard",
      "status": "in-progress",  // done | in-progress | blocked | outstanding | addressed
      "frontmatter": { ... },   // raw YAML frontmatter fields preserved for the inspector
      "githubIssue": "...",     // optional — hoisted from frontmatter when present
      "linearIssueIdentifier": "..." // optional — hoisted from frontmatter when present
    }
  ],
  "edges": [
    {
      "from": "SPEC-016",
      "to": "US-001",
      "kind": "contains"        // contains | depends_on
    }
  ]
}
```

**How the graph is built.** `graph-engine.mjs:buildGraph(planrDir)` tries the CLI
delegate path first (A.1: `planr graph --json` or `planr status --json`, requires
CLI >= v1.7.2). If unavailable, the native reader (`graph-reader.mjs:readGraph`)
walks `.planr/` and assembles an equivalent graph. Both paths validate against
`schemas/v1.0.0/graph.schema.json` before returning.

**Spec-vs-code comparison.** The spec (FR2 / US-002) requires node types
`epic | feature | story | task | spec | backlog | quick | sprint | adr` and edge
kinds `contains` and `depends_on`. The code matches exactly — the schema enum
contains all nine types and both edge kinds. Status classification matches the
spec's five values.

**Known drift — loose `.planr/*.md` files surfaced as nodes.** See [Drift
findings](#drift-findings) at the bottom of this file.

---

## GET /api/node/:id

Returns a single artifact with its markdown body included. Used by the Detail
view to populate the full inspector pane.

**Path parameter.** `:id` is the artifact id (e.g. `SPEC-016`, `US-002`,
`T-007`). URL-decoding is applied.

**Response** — `200 application/json`:

```
{
  "id": "T-007",
  "type": "task",
  "title": "Shell wiring: hash router, theme persistence...",
  "status": "outstanding",
  "frontmatter": { "storyId": "US-003", "dependsOn": ["T-006"], ... },
  "body": "# T-007 — ...\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n..."
}
```

The `body` field is the raw markdown below the frontmatter fence — this is how
the Detail view renders Gherkin criteria and subtask checkboxes.

**Response on missing id** — `404 application/json`:

```
{ "error": "unknown node \"<id>\"" }
```

**Spec-vs-code comparison.** The spec (US-008 AC3) says the Detail view data is
assembled from `GET /api/node/:id` with the full node including frontmatter and
body. The code matches: `getNode` always uses the native reader (never the CLI
delegate), because the CLI output does not include markdown bodies. This is an
intentional implementation choice not mentioned explicitly in the spec, but it
satisfies the AC.

---

## GET /api/meta

Returns server metadata consumed by the shell breadcrumb and version chip.

**Response** — `200 application/json`:

```
{
  "version": "0.21.0",
  "planrDir": "/path/to/.planr",
  "views": ["overview", "graph", "board", "list", "sprints", "activity"],
  "defaultView": "overview"
}
```

**Spec-vs-code comparison.** This route is not mentioned in the spec's FR list or
the US-001 acceptance criteria, but it was added in T-007 to support the shell's
breadcrumb and version chip. It is an additive implementation — the spec does not
conflict with it.

## GET /api/events

An SSE (Server-Sent Events) stream. The server keeps this connection open and
pushes events as `.planr/` files change (unless `--no-watch` was passed).

**Response headers:**

```
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Cache-Control: no-cache
Connection: keep-alive
```

**First event on connect** — named `ready`:

```
event: ready
data: {"ok":true,"pid":<pid>}
```

**Subsequent patch events** — default `message` type, one per debounced batch of
file changes:

```
data: {"updated":[...],"added":[...],"removed":[...],"edges":{"added":[...],"removed":[...]}}
```

Each patch has the shape:

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|-------|------|---------|
| `updated` | `Node[]` | Nodes whose content changed since the last patch |
| `added` | `Node[]` | Nodes that did not exist in the previous snapshot |
| `removed` | `string[]` | Node ids no longer present in the graph |
| `edges.added` | `Edge[]` | New edges |
| `edges.removed` | `Edge[]` | Removed edges |

**On disconnect.** When the client closes the connection, `req.on('close')` removes
the response from the `sseClients` Set so the watcher does not try to write to a
closed stream.

**When `--no-watch` is passed.** The stream still returns the initial `ready` event,
then emits no further messages.

**Spec-vs-code comparison.** US-004 AC3 says patches must be pushed as minimal
diffs. The code implements this exactly via `watcher.mjs:diffGraphs`. US-004 AC6
says the client must merge without resetting state — `main.js:mergePatch` handles
this in place without remounting or rerouting.

## GET /health

Lightweight liveness probe used by the reuse-if-running detection in
`procedures/dashboard-preflight.md`.

**Response** — `200 application/json`:

```
{ "ok": true, "pid": <number> }
```

**Spec-vs-code comparison.** US-001 AC3 requires reuse detection. The spec does
not name this specific route, but `commands/dashboard.md` and
`procedures/dashboard-preflight.md` both prescribe a `GET /health` probe. The
code matches.

---

## GET /*

Serves static files from `lib/dashboard/app/`. Requests for `/` or unknown paths
fall through to `index.html`. Path traversal (e.g. `../../etc/passwd`) is blocked:
the resolved absolute path is checked to remain within the app directory.

**Response** — `200` with the appropriate MIME type, or `404`/`403` on missing or
blocked paths.

## Drift findings

### Known limitation: native reader surfaces loose `.planr/*.md` files as nodes

**Spec intent.** FR2 describes the graph as built from named artifact types in their
canonical directories: epics in `.planr/epics/`, specs in `.planr/specs/SPEC-*/`,
stories in `.planr/stories/`, etc. The "Notes for Decomposition" section uses the
directory layout to define what constitutes a graph node.

**Implementation behavior.** `graph-reader.mjs:walkArtifacts` performs a full
recursive walk of `.planr/` with no directory allowlist. Any `.md` file anywhere
under `.planr/` — including loose files like `.planr/ESTIMATION.md`,
`.planr/checklists/AGILE-DEVELOPMENT-GUIDE.md`, or future planning documents
placed at the root level — will be ingested as a node. Because these files either
lack a frontmatter `id` field or have ids that do not match the `PREFIX-NNN`
pattern, they are assigned a fallback id derived from their filename and assigned
type `spec` (the `inferType` default for unrecognized directory names). This can
produce unexpected entries in the graph: a file like `.planr/ESTIMATION.md`
appears as a `spec` node titled "ESTIMATION" with status `outstanding`.

**Specifically for `Spec` nodes.** The spec says Spec nodes correspond to
`.planr/specs/SPEC-NNN-*/SPEC-*.md` root files. The native reader would also
surface story and task files inside those spec directories as `story` and `task`
nodes (correctly), but it would additionally surface any other `.md` file placed
inside a spec directory that is not itself a spec root, story, or task — for
example a design document, a QA report, or a qa-report.md file. The reader does
skip `-error-report.md` and `-gherkin.feature` files explicitly, but not
`qa-report.md` files — these appear as `spec` nodes as well.

**Impact.** The CLI delegate path (`planr graph --json`) does not have this issue
because it uses the CLI's own artifact registry, which is scoped to known
directories. This means the two paths — while validated against the same schema —
can produce different node sets on a real project, in violation of the
"one engine, one truth" business rule (BR2). The equivalence conformance test
(`tests/dashboard/graph-equivalence.test.mjs`) passes because the shared fixture
in `conformance/fixtures/dashboard-graph/` contains only correctly-structured
artifacts with no loose files, so the drift does not appear under controlled
conditions.

**Recommended fix (not in this release).** Add a directory allowlist to
`walkArtifacts` — only traverse `epics/`, `features/`, `stories/`, `tasks/`,
`sprints/`, `backlog/`, `quick/`, `adrs/`, and `specs/` (with the further
refinement that inside a `specs/SPEC-NNN-*/` directory, only the spec root file,
`stories/*.md`, and `tasks/*.md` are included). Alternatively, add a filter that
requires nodes to have a frontmatter `id` field matching the `PREFIX-NNN` pattern
before inclusion.

### T-001 main.js: stub vs. full router

The T-001 task description stated that `main.js` would be "a stub with no view
logic yet (views are T-003)." T-003 does not exist in the final task list; T-006
owns the final `main.js`. The delivered `main.js` is the full router, SSE
connector, `filterState`, and `cmdkDispatcher`. The QA report flags this as a
non-blocking rationale residue; the implementation is correct and the acceptance
criteria are satisfied.

### `/api/meta` route not in spec

The `/api/meta` route is an additive implementation. It was added in T-007 to
give the client shell a server-side source of truth for the views list, the
default view, the plugin version, and the planr directory path. Nothing in the
spec conflicts with this route, but it was not listed in the spec's FR table or
in any US acceptance criterion.
